name: Assembly Order Planner
blurb: assembly order and access needs as a step list
intro: Paste the parts, one per line, with what each goes onto and optionally the tool, approach direction and time. It sorts them into a buildable order (a topological sort), keeps covers until the parts behind them are in, and counts tool changes and turn-overs, the two things design-for-assembly tries to minimise.

usage: Give text: one part per line as 'part -> part it goes onto, another | tool: name | from: top/bottom/front/back/left/right/side | time: 30s | blocks: top | note: …' (only the part name is required; # starts a comment) and strategy 'group' (fewest turn-overs and tool changes) or 'input' (listed order where possible). It returns the ordered step table, counts of tool changes, reorientations, dependency levels and total time, access conflicts and circular dependencies as warnings, and the steps as text plus a Mermaid dependency graph. Use it to plan or check a build sequence and write work instructions.
sources: Kahn, 'Topological sorting of large networks', CACM 1962 (ordering algorithm)
Boothroyd, Dewhurst and Knight, 'Product Design for Manufacture and Assembly' (minimise reorientations and tool changes)
